hits.text:
this harness engineering paper is required reading if you run Claude Code

Wavestone AI Lab read the source code of 11 coding agents, Claude Code and Codex included, and found the same 7-part harness inside every good one

agent = model + harness

the 7 parts, smallest version to largest:
> loop - a plain while loop up to fully replayable runs
> LLM layer - one prompt template up to 29 provider profiles
> tools - bash alone up to 43 typed tools loaded on demand
> memory - raw history up to notes that survive between sessions
> safety - a step limit up to rules, a reviewer model and a sandbox
> orchestration - Aider skips sub-agents, the rest fork them
> extensions - SKILL. md in 9 of the 11, MCP in 8

the pages to open first:
> p.4 - the full 7-part map
> p.12 - three loop types, with Claude Code and Codex as examples
> p.67 - 18 design rules
> p.71 - a 90-line harness that covers all 7 parts

the model gets the headlines
the harness decides whether the agent finishes the job

engineers who can draw these 7 parts on a whiteboard are the ones getting hired to build agents

the complete guide to harnesses that hold up under real work is below 👇

the core idea: the vault is the loop's state, not the chat window

everything Claude Code remembers lives in a .md file - the Karpathy-style second brain, now wired to run itself

the loop:
> capture - a thought drops into 00-inbox
> context - Opus 5.5 pulls links, tags and nearby notes
> draft - Sonnet 5.5 edits inside a git worktree, never the live vault
> review - a Haiku 5.5 critic reads the diff before anything ships
> commit - appended to the vault, nothing gets rewritten

the key insight: frontmatter fields like supports, contradicts and supersedes are graph edges, not metadata

the note format itself is the write API. the second brain compounds on top of it

start with a plain loop. it runs about 2-4x a direct call

> switch to a full graph only when state has to outlive the session
> or when several agents need to coordinate
> or when you need to explain what changed
> that jump can run 10-50x

one review assistant walked from 55% to 72% to 84% just by climbing through these shapes in order

4 AI analysts independently examine fundamentals, technical indicators, financial news and market sentiment
